name: Central Intelligence Agency
kicker: U.S. foreign intelligence agency · Created by the National Security Act, 1947
briefing: The Central Intelligence Agency gathers secret information about other countries to help U.S. presidents make decisions, and it sometimes carries out covert operations overseas. It was created in 1947 by the National Security Act, which Harry Truman signed, and grew out of World War II’s Office of Strategic Services. Based in Langley, Virginia, it ran the U-2 spy plane program in the 1950s and planned the failed Bay of Pigs invasion of Cuba in 1961.
answerHtml: Central Intelligence Agency (accept CIA; prompt on Langley or the Company; do not accept “FBI” or “NSA”)
reject: office of the director of national intelligence

qb.tip: Search QBReader for this answer line (Middle School + Easy High School, power-marked) to see how real tossups clue it.

tossups.p: Rear Admiral Roscoe Hillenkoetter [“HILL-en-ket-er”] served as the first director of this agency from 1947 to 1950. The same 1947 law that created this agency also created the National Security Council and made the Air Force a separate branch of the military.
tossups.r: That law was the National Security Act, signed by Harry Truman. For 10 points, name this spy agency headquartered in Langley, Virginia.

tossups.p: William “Wild Bill” Donovan, who had won the Medal of Honor in World War I, led the World War II spy service from which this agency grew. Harry Truman broke up that wartime service, the Office of Strategic Services, in 1945.
tossups.r: Two years later, Truman signed the law that created this agency. For 10 points, name this foreign intelligence agency based in Langley, Virginia.

tossups.p: Allen Dulles, whose brother John Foster Dulles was Secretary of State, became this agency’s longest-serving director, leading it from 1953 to 1961. John F. Kennedy forced Dulles out after a failed invasion this agency had planned.
tossups.r: That invasion landed at Cuba’s Bay of Pigs. For 10 points, name this American spy agency.

tossups.p: In 1953, Kermit Roosevelt Jr., a grandson of Theodore Roosevelt, led this agency’s operation to help overthrow Iran’s prime minister, Mohammad Mosaddegh [“moh-sah-DEK”]. The next year, this agency backed a coup that drove Guatemala’s president, Jacobo Árbenz [“AR-bens”], from power.
tossups.r: For 10 points, name this U.S. spy agency created in 1947 and based in Langley, Virginia.

tossups.p: Richard Bissell ran this agency’s program to build and fly a high-altitude spy plane, which began test flights in Nevada in 1955. In 1960, one of those planes was shot down over the Soviet Union, and its pilot, Francis Gary Powers, was captured.
tossups.r: That plane was the U-2. For 10 points, name this American spy agency, which also planned the Bay of Pigs invasion.

tossups.p: In 1962, Francis Gary Powers was traded for the Soviet spy Rudolf Abel on Berlin’s Glienicke [“GLEE-nih-kuh”] Bridge, a story told in the Steven Spielberg film _Bridge of Spies_. Powers had been flying a spy plane for this agency when he was shot down.
tossups.r: That spy plane was the U-2. For 10 points, name this American spy agency headquartered in Langley, Virginia.

tossups.p: This agency trained about 1,400 Cuban exiles of Brigade 2506 under a plan drawn up during Dwight Eisenhower’s presidency. In April 1961, those exiles landed at Playa Girón [“hee-ROHN”] and were defeated within days by Fidel Castro’s forces.
tossups.r: That landing was the Bay of Pigs invasion. For 10 points, name this U.S. spy agency.

tossups.p: In 1975, a Senate committee led by Frank Church of Idaho investigated this agency’s secret plots to kill foreign leaders such as Fidel Castro. The next year, Gerald Ford issued an executive order banning political assassinations by U.S. government employees.
tossups.r: For 10 points, name this spy agency created by the National Security Act of 1947.

tossups.p: After Gerald Ford dismissed William Colby as this agency’s director in 1975, Ford chose a future president to lead it in 1976 and 1977. In 1999, this agency’s headquarters was named for that man.
tossups.r: That man was George H. W. Bush. For 10 points, name this spy agency based in Langley, Virginia.

tossups.p: Jim Sanborn’s sculpture _Kryptos_, which holds four coded messages, stands outside this agency’s headquarters, and its last message resisted solvers for decades. Inside, a Bible verse in the lobby reads, “And ye shall know the truth, and the truth shall make you free.”
tossups.r: Stars on its Memorial Wall honor officers who died in its service. For 10 points, name this spy agency whose headquarters is in Langley, Virginia.

tossups.p: A copy of Bela Pratt’s statue of a Revolutionary War spy, whose original stands at Yale, was placed at this agency’s headquarters. A statue of William Donovan, who led this agency’s World War II forerunner, stands in its lobby.
tossups.r: The Revolutionary War spy was Nathan Hale. For 10 points, name this American spy agency created in 1947.

tossups.p: James Jesus Angleton led this agency’s counterintelligence staff for twenty years, searching for Soviet moles inside it. Long after Angleton left, one of this agency’s officers, Aldrich Ames, was arrested in 1994 for spying for the Soviet Union and Russia.
tossups.r: For 10 points, name this American spy agency based in Langley, Virginia, which ran the U-2 program.

tossups.p: In 1980, this agency’s officer Tony Mendez helped six American diplomats escape from Iran by disguising them as a Canadian film crew scouting locations for a fake science-fiction movie. Ben Affleck directed and starred in a 2012 film about that rescue.
tossups.r: That film was _Argo_. For 10 points, name this American spy agency headquartered in Langley, Virginia.

tossups.p: During the Vietnam War, this agency secretly owned an airline called Air America, which flew supplies for a secret war in Laos in which Hmong [“MONG”] fighters battled communist forces. This agency is often nicknamed “the Company.”
tossups.r: For 10 points, name this American spy agency, which has no police powers inside the United States, unlike the FBI.

tossups.p: After the 9/11 attacks, a 2004 law created a Director of National Intelligence, ending this agency’s director’s role as head of the U.S. intelligence community. This agency’s officers later tracked Osama bin Laden to Abbottabad [“AB-uh-tuh-bahd”], Pakistan.
tossups.r: He was killed there in a 2011 raid by U.S. Navy SEALs. For 10 points, name this American spy agency based in Langley, Virginia.

trap.title: Which three letters?
trap.body: Several agencies get mixed up. The CIA gathers intelligence abroad and has no police powers at home; the FBI, part of the Justice Department, investigates federal crimes and spies inside the United States; and the NSA intercepts and decodes communications. The CIA’s World War II forerunner was the Office of Strategic Services (OSS), and the Soviet Union’s spy agency was the KGB.
trap.fix: Spying abroad, Langley, the OSS, Allen Dulles, the U-2, the Bay of Pigs, and the Church Committee mean the CIA. J. Edgar Hoover, G-men, and the Ten Most Wanted list mean the FBI. If the question asks for “this law,” the answer may be the National Security Act of 1947.
trap.line: Real answer line: Central Intelligence Agency (accept CIA; prompt on Langley or the Company; do not accept “FBI” or “NSA”)
